gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 13 build already compiles the landed devres helper packet, so this lane can keep MMIO-facing reviewability tied to the same bounded replay path as the other helper anchors.
The existing make target keeps the helper-first devres survey packet runnable through the same repeatable checkpoint as the rest of the Phase 13 tranche.

The landed helper lab already mirrors the bounded __devm_ioremap() lifetime split, keeps the direct devm_ioremap_wc() wrapper explicit as a pure write-combined lifetime planner, preserves exact devm_iounmap() pointer matching, and stays inside the helper-first posture the roadmap allows.

Dedicated devres tests keep the current helper-only packet honest around managed acquire cleanup, the direct devm_ioremap_wc() wrapper success and map-failure cleanup path, resource-backed planning, devm_of_iomap() size reporting, WC memtype reservation shaping, and arch phys WC release-token bookkeeping.
The slice note records the narrow helper-first boundary so this lane does not overstate itself as live devres, MMIO, or device-tree parity.
The dedicated reviewability gate keeps the helper-only DMA/scatterlist boundary machine-checkable instead of leaving that packet implied only by prose or shared build wiring.

The dedicated coherent-DMA replay proves the manifest still records the shipped devres test, reviewability gate, and survey evidence while keeping the live DMA-backed helper and scatterlist ownership boundary explicit.
The survey note now makes the roadmap gap explicit by naming the landed MMIO-adjacent planners together with the live-state boundaries that still remain blocked.

The helper lab already carries the bounded __devm_ioremap_resource() planner for memory-backed resource checks, inclusive size calculation, pretty-name shaping, busy-region failures, and remap cleanup without claiming live reservations.
The landed devm_of_iomap() planner keeps translated-resource selection, optional size reporting, and downstream planner failure shaping reviewable before any live device-tree ownership is attempted.
The current devres helper keeps detach-time arch_io_free_memtype_wc() bookkeeping and failure shaping reviewable while live arch memtype mutation stays outside the shipped packet.

The helper lab now carries one tiny devm_arch_phys_wc_add() token-style planner that captures release-token retention on success, release-record cleanup on failure, and detach-time arch_phys_wc_del() intent without claiming live arch memtype side effects.
Live MMIO side effects remain blocked because the roadmap still wants Phase 13 devres work to stay helper-first and reviewable instead of claiming real region mutation or address-space effects.

Live DMA-backed helpers remain blocked because the current packet does not claim dmam_alloc_* coverage, does not model dma_map_sgtable() or unmap flows, and must stay helper-first instead of pretending to own real DMA mapping state.
Live scatterlist ownership remains blocked because the current helper packet does not model struct scatterlist traversal, sg_table lifecycle, or broader sg_* ownership transfer.
Live device-tree walking remains blocked because the current devm_of_iomap() slice only models translated-resource selection by index and should not pretend to own OF lookup or node lifetime.
Live arch memtype state remains blocked because the current WC helpers stop at bookkeeping and error shaping rather than mutating the real arch memtype token or release path.
